docs.title: Setup and requirements
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: This document lists the tools you need to build Gitea from source and how to get the code. Once your environment is ready, see development.md for the build and development workflow, and testing.md for running tests.

docs.title: Go
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Requirements > Go
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Install Go and set up your Go environment. The required version is the one declared in go.mod; installing the same version your continuous integration uses avoids gofmt differences between Go releases.

docs.title: Node.js and pnpm
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Requirements > Node.js and pnpm
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Install Node.js to build the JavaScript and CSS files. The minimum supported version is the one declared in package.json (engines.node); the latest LTS is recommended.

docs.title: Make
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Requirements > Make
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Gitea uses Make to drive builds, linting, and tests. On Windows it can be installed via MSYS2 or Chocolatey.

docs.title: Python with uv (optional)
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Requirements > Python with uv (optional)
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Linting the templates, workflow files, and YAML requires Python tooling that Gitea runs through uv. After installing uv, make creates the environment automatically (uv sync); you only need this if you run make lint-templates, make lint-yaml, or make lint-actions locally.

docs.title: Getting the source code
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Getting the source code
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: To contribute changes, fork the repository on GitHub and add your fork as a git remote so you can push branches and open pull requests. See GitHub's working with forks documentation for the details.

docs.title: Installing dependencies
docs.heading_path: Setup and requirements > Installing dependencies
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Most build and test targets install the dependencies they need on their own. To fetch everything up front, run make deps (or the per-group make deps-frontend, make deps-backend, make deps-tools, make deps-py).

docs.title: Prepare build environment
docs.heading_path: Prepare build environment
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Complete the steps in build-setup.md to prepare your environment for building Gitea from source.

docs.title: Choose a branch
docs.heading_path: Prepare build environment > Choose a branch
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: By default, the cloned repository is on main branch (the current development branch for next major release, aka: main nightly).

docs.snippet: - bindata: Build a single monolithic binary, with all assets included. Required for distribution and production build. - pam: Enable support for PAM (Linux Pluggable Authentication Modules).  Can be used to authenticate local users or extend authentication to methods available…

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Gitea will search for a number of things from the _CustomPath_. By default, this is the custom/ directory in the current working directory when running Gitea. It will also look for its configuration file _CustomConf_ in $(CustomPath)/conf/app.ini, and will use the current…

docs.snippet: A PR should only be assigned to a milestone if it will likely be merged into the given version. \ PRs without a milestone may not be merged.

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - modifies/…: Determines which parts of the codebase are affected. These labels will be set through the CI. - topic/…: Determines the conceptual component of Gitea that is affected, i.e. issues, projects, or authentication. At best, PRs should only target one component but there…

docs.title: Reviewing PRs
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Reviewing PRs
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Maintainers are encouraged to review pull requests in areas where they have expertise or particular interest.

docs.title: For reviewers
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Reviewing PRs > For reviewers
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - **Verification**: Verify that the PR accurately reflects the changes, and verify that the tests and documentation are complete and aligned with the implementation. - **Actionable feedback**: Say what should change and why, and distinguish required changes from optional…

docs.title: Getting PRs merged
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Getting PRs merged
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Changes to Gitea must be reviewed before they are accepted, including changes from owners and maintainers. The exception is critical bugs that prevent Gitea from compiling or starting.

docs.title: Final call
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Final call
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If a PR has been ignored for more than 7 days with no comments or reviews, and the author or any maintainer believes it will not survive a long wait (such as a refactoring PR), they can send "final call" to the TOC by mentioning them in a comment.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Commit messages
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Mergers are required to rewrite the PR title and the first comment (the summary) when necessary so the squash commit message is clear. Usually the Pull Request description and commit message body should not be empty, unless the title is already clear enough or the description…

docs.title: PR Co-authors
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Code review > Commit messages > PR Co-authors
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: A person counts as a PR co-author once they (co-)authored a commit that is not simply a Merge base branch into branch commit. Mergers must remove such false-positive co-authors when writing the squash message. Every true co-author must remain in the commit message.

docs.title: Review expectations
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Maintainers > Review expectations
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Every PR **must** be reviewed by at least two maintainers (or owners) before merge. **Exception:** after one week, refactoring PRs and documentation-only PRs need only one maintainer approval.

docs.title: Becoming a maintainer
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Maintainers > Becoming a maintainer
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: A maintainer should already be a Gitea contributor with at least four merged PRs. To apply, use the Discord #develop channel. Maintainer teams may also invite contributors.

docs.title: Stepping down, advisors, and inactivity
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Maintainers > Stepping down, advisors, and inactivity
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If you cannot keep reviewing, apply to leave the maintainers team. You can join the advisors team; advisors who want to review again are welcome back as maintainers.

docs.title: Account security
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Maintainers > Account security
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: For security, maintainers should enable 2FA and sign commits with GPG when possible:

docs.title: Mergers

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Mergers are the maintainers who carry out the final merge of approved PRs. Their responsibilities, described throughout this guide, are:

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: A merger must already be a Gitea maintainer. To apply, use the Discord #maintainers channel. The minimum requirement for applications to become a merger is to have participated actively in the community for at least four months before applying. Ultimately, regardless of previous…

docs.title: Technical Oversight Committee (TOC)
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Technical Oversight Committee (TOC)
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: At the start of 2023, the Owners team was dissolved. Instead, the governance charter proposed a technical oversight committee (TOC) which expands the ownership team of the Gitea project from three elected positions to six positions. Three positions are elected as it has been…

docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Contribution Roles > Technical Oversight Committee (TOC) > TOC election process
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Any maintainer is eligible to be part of the community TOC if they are not associated with the Gitea company. A maintainer can either nominate themselves, or can be nominated by other maintainers to be a candidate for the TOC election. If you are nominated by someone else, you…

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Each member of the community elected TOC will be granted $500 each month as compensation for their work.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.heading_path: Community governance and review process > Roadmap
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Each year a roadmap will be discussed with the entire Gitea maintainers team, and feedback will be solicited from various stakeholders. TOC members need to review the roadmap every year and work together on the direction of the project.

docs.title: Development
docs.heading_path: Development
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: This document describes how to build Gitea from source and the day-to-day development workflow. For prerequisites and how to obtain the code, see build-setup.md. For running tests, see testing.md. For the contribution workflow and review process, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Building
docs.heading_path: Development > Building
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: No build tags are required: SQLite support is compiled in by default, which is enough for local development. The build target runs two sub-targets, frontend and backend. The bindata tag embeds the frontend assets into the binary and is only needed when packaging a self-contained…

docs.title: or watch only the backend (Go)
docs.heading_path: or watch only the backend (Go)
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Watching all backend source files may hit the default open-files limit on macOS or Linux; raise it with ulimit -n 12288` for the current shell, or in your shell startup file to make it permanent.

docs.title: Formatting, linting and checks
docs.heading_path: or watch only the backend (Go) > Formatting, linting and checks
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Continuous integration rejects pull requests that fail formatting, linting, or consistency checks. Format your code first:

docs.title: or only one side
docs.heading_path: or only one side
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Many linters can fix issues automatically with make lint-fix (or the scoped make lint-backend-fix / make lint-frontend-fix). The combined consistency checks that CI runs are available as make checks`.

docs.title: Building and adding SVGs
docs.heading_path: or only one side > Building and adding SVGs
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: SVG icons are built with make svg, which compiles the icon sources into public/assets/img/svg. Custom icons can be added under web_src/svg.

docs.title: Updating the API
docs.heading_path: or only one side > Updating the API
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: When you create or change API routes, you **must** update the Swagger documentation using go-swagger comments. See the backend development guidelines for how API routes, request/response structs, and swagger definitions fit together.

docs.title: Creating new configuration options
docs.heading_path: or only one side > Creating new configuration options
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: When adding configuration options it is not enough to add them to the modules/setting files. Also update custom/conf/app.example.ini, and document them in the configuration cheat sheet, which lives in the documentation repository.

docs.title: Database migrations
docs.heading_path: or only one side > Database migrations
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: If you make breaking changes to a database-persisted struct under models/, add a new migration in modelmigration/. See testing.md for running the migration tests.

docs.title: Visual Studio Code

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: A launch.json and tasks.json are provided in contrib/development/vscode. See contrib/development/README.md for details.

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: The backend is written in Go. Web routing is handled by chi and database access goes through the XORM ORM. Understanding how the packages depend on each other is essential before contributing backend code.

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - Top-level packages use the plural form: services, models, routers. - Subpackages use the singular form: services/user, models/repository.

docs.title: Dependencies

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Pull requests should only modify go.mod and go.sum where it relates to the change at hand, be it a bug fix or a new feature. Otherwise, these files should only be touched by pull requests whose sole purpose is updating dependencies. Run make tidy after any change to go.mod.

docs.snippet: The frontend uses Vue 3, hard-forked Fomantic-UI (built on jQuery) and Tailwind CSS. Pages are rendered with Go HTML templates. Source files live in:

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Frontend dependencies are managed with pnpm. The same rules as for backend dependencies apply, except the relevant files are package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, and new versions must always reference an existing published version.

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Mixing frameworks arbitrarily makes code hard to maintain. Recommended combinations:

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - Keep features in their own files or directories. - Use kebab-case for HTML ids and classes with 2-3 feature keywords. - Prefix classes to avoid short-name conflicts between different frameworks. - Our framework can automatically link "input" and "label" if they are the…

docs.title: CSS
docs.heading_path: Frontend development guidelines > CSS
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Prefer Tailwind utility classes with the tw- prefix, and the flex-* layout helpers over per-child margins. Gitea also ships a small set of custom helpers: gt- for general helpers and g- for framework-level helpers (see web_src/css/helpers.css); use these only when a Tailwind…

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - Use import type for type-only imports. - Use the ! non-null assertion (rather than ?./??) when a value is known to always exist. - Only mark a function async when it actually uses await or returns a Promise.  Avoid async event listeners; if unavoidable, call e.preventDefault()…

docs.title: Data fetching

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh

docs.title: DOM attributes

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Avoid node.dataset because of its camel-casing behavior; use node.getAttribute in new code. Never bind user-provided data directly onto DOM nodes.

docs.title: Showing and hiding elements
docs.heading_path: Frontend development guidelines > Showing and hiding elements
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - In Vue, use v-if and v-show. If an element contains unmanaged DOM, use v-show to avoid losing the DOM state. - In Go templates and plain JavaScript, use the .tw-hidden class together with the  showElem(), hideElem(), and toggleElem() helpers from  web_src/js/utils/dom.ts.

docs.title: UI component gallery
docs.heading_path: Frontend development guidelines > UI component gallery
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: When running Gitea in development mode, standardized UI components are available at /devtest (for example http://localhost:3000/devtest). These pages are also used by the e2e tests.

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Gitea is a large, long-lived project. Over time the codebase has accumulated outdated mechanisms, mixed frameworks, and legacy code that can cause bugs or slow down new features. Refactoring keeps the codebase maintainable, but it needs to be done carefully so it improves things…

docs.snippet: - Be forward-looking: address the root cause, not just the immediate symptom. - Aim to reduce ambiguity and conflicts and to improve maintainability. - Explain the rationale in the PR description: why the refactor is necessary, how it  resolves the legacy problem, and its…

docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: - Keep refactoring PRs short-lived (typically no more than 7 days) with quick review  cycles, and merge them promptly so they do not block on unrelated work. - A non-author core member may approve and merge a refactoring PR after 7 days if the  TOC has raised no objection. -…

docs.snippet: This document describes the release cycle, backports, versioning, and the release manager checklist. For everyday contribution workflow, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.snippet: - Aim for a major release about every three or four months. - Roughly two or three months of general development, then about one month of testing and polish called the **release freeze**. - *Starting with v1.26 the release cycle will be more predictable and follow a more regular…

docs.snippet: - Merge feature PRs before the freeze when you can. - Feature PRs still open at the freeze move to the next milestone. Watch Discord for the freeze announcement. - During the freeze, a **release branch** takes fixes backported from main. Release candidates ship for testing; the…

docs.title: Patch releases
docs.heading_path: Release management > Release Cycle > Patch releases
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: During a cycle we may ship patch releases for an older line. For example, if the latest release is v1.2, we can still publish v1.1.1 after v1.1.0.

docs.snippet: We support per standard the last major release. For example, if the latest release is v1.26, we support v1.26 and v1.25, but not v1.24 anymore. We will only publish security fixes for the last major release, so if you are using an older release, please upgrade to a supported…

docs.title: Testing
docs.heading_path: Testing
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Gitea has four kinds of automated tests: backend unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end (e2e) tests, and migration tests. Local runs default to SQLite, so no extra services are required to get started.

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.heading_path: Testing > Unit tests
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Backend unit tests live in *_test.go files next to the code they cover. Set GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1 to log all SQL statements executed during the tests.

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.heading_path: single file: > Integration tests
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Integration tests exercise Gitea against a real database. They live in tests/integration/ and require Git LFS to be installed. The database is selected with GITEA_TEST_DATABASE; an empty value defaults to SQLite, which needs no external service:

docs.title: Running against other databases
docs.heading_path: single file: > Integration tests > Running against other databases
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: Set GITEA_TEST_DATABASE together with the matching TEST_* connection variables. The commands below start a throwaway database container (press Ctrl-C to stop and remove it) and then run the tests against it.

docs.title: MySQL
docs.heading_path: single file: > Integration tests > Running against other databases > MySQL
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: bash docker run -e "MYSQL_DATABASE=test" -e "MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes" -p 3306:3306 --rm --name mysql mysql:latest

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.heading_path: single file: > Integration tests > Running against other databases > PostgreSQL
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: bash docker run -e "POSTGRES_DB=test" -e "POSTGRES_USER=postgres" -e "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres" -p 5432:5432 --rm --name pgsql postgres:latest docker run --rm -p 9000:9000 -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=123456 -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=12345678 --name minio bitnamilegacy/minio:2023.8.31

docs.title: MSSQL
docs.heading_path: single file: > Integration tests > Running against other databases > MSSQL
docs.attribution: © go-gitea/gitea contributors — MIT License, via docs-mesh
docs.snippet: bash docker run -e "ACCEPT_EULA=Y" -e "MSSQL_PID=Standard" -e "SA_PASSWORD=MwantsaSecurePassword1" -p 1433:1433 --rm --name mssql microsoft/mssql-server-linux:latest
